html:
Gambling has been legal in Macau since the 1840s, but the city became the world's largest gambling centre after the government ended the casino monopoly in 2002 and let in foreign firms.

For forty years before that the licence belonged to one company, led by the tycoon Stanley Ho. After the handover, the new government opened the market. Las Vegas firms built huge resorts, many on land reclaimed between two islands, and mainland Chinese visitors came by the millions after travel rules were eased. By 2007 Macau's gambling income was larger than that of Las Vegas.

Casino taxes pay for most of the government and give Macau one of the highest incomes per head in the world. Beijing has pushed the city to depend less on gambling, and a crackdown on junket operators who brought in high rollers ended many in the 2020s. The bridge from Hong Kong opened in 2018, and crowds of visitors fill the old centre around the Ruins of Saint Paul's.
sum: Gambling has been legal in Macau since the 1840s, but the city became the world's largest gambling centre after the government ended the casino monopoly in 2002 and let in foreign firms.
